# Cert Jenna

> Cert Jenna is a single-page, fully client-side web tool that generates self-signed X.509 certificates for local development. Keys are created in the browser with the Web Crypto API and downloaded as a ZIP. No server, no account, no network requests.

It is a joke-flavoured front end for a practical idea: get a usable `server.crt` / `server.key` pair for `my-app.local` in two clicks, without installing mkcert or remembering `openssl req` flags. Everything happens in the page, and private keys never leave the tab except through the download button.

The wordmark on the page styles the name as Cert(ificate) Jenna(rator). That is decoration; the application is called Cert Jenna.

## Tool

- [Cert Jenna](https://bitbronze.github.io/cert-jenna/): the generator itself. Enter an app name, then pick Gen Simple or Gen Complete.

## Modes

- **Gen Simple** — downloads `server.crt` and `server.key`. The server certificate is signed by a root CA that is generated and then discarded, so the bundle contains no issuing certificate and nothing can chain or verify against it. Intended for throwaway local TLS.
- **Gen Complete** — downloads `root.crt`, `root.key`, `server.crt`, `server.key`, `client.crt` and `client.key`. The root is a real CA certificate you can import into a trust store, and the server and client leaves chain to it. Also usable for mutual TLS testing.

Output arrives as a ZIP named `<app-name>-simple.zip` or `<app-name>-complete.zip`.

## Technical details

- Key algorithm: RSA 2048-bit, public exponent 65537, signatures over RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256 (`1.2.840.113549.1.1.11`).
- Certificates are PEM-encoded DER; private keys are exported as PKCS#8 PEM (`-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`).
- Subject and issuer distinguished names contain a single `CN` (UTF8String) attribute and nothing else — no O, OU, C, ST or L.
- Certificates are X.509 version 3 and carry only four extensions:
  - Basic Constraints (critical): `CA:TRUE` on the root, `CA:FALSE` on leaves. No path length constraint.
  - Key Usage (critical): `keyCertSign, cRLSign` on the root; `digitalSignature, keyEncipherment` on the server leaf; `digitalSignature` on the client leaf.
  - Subject Alternative Name (non-critical): one `dNSName` entry, emitted only when the app name is a syntactically valid DNS name. The client certificate never carries a SAN.
  - Extended Key Usage (non-critical): `serverAuth` on the server leaf, `clientAuth` on the client leaf. The root carries no EKU.
- Validity: 36500 days (100 years) for the root and leaves. `notBefore` is set one day before generation time to tolerate clock skew. Dates from 2050 onward are encoded as `GeneralizedTime`, earlier dates as `UTCTime`.
- Serial numbers are 16 random bytes with the sign bit cleared.
- The ZIP container is written by hand in the page: stored entries, no compression, CRC-32 checksums, UTF-8 filename flag.

## Known limitations

- No Subject Key Identifier, Authority Key Identifier or CRL Distribution Points are emitted, so strict chain validators may warn.
- No OCSP or CRL support, and nothing is installed into a trust store automatically.
- RSA only — no ECDSA or Ed25519.
- One app name per run; it becomes the CN and, when valid, the SAN.
- Web Crypto requires a secure context, so generation only works over HTTPS or on `localhost`.
- Gen Simple output cannot be trusted by anything, including by adding it to a trust store, because its issuing root is never written to the ZIP.
